structural_rules.rule: Resolve HOME (cmd package resolve-activity --brief -a android.intent.action.MAIN -c android.intent.category.HOME). Never disable that package, nor any other enabled package that has a HOME activity, nor the FallbackHome in com.android.tv.settings.
structural_rules.why: B3 B4 B6 B7 B8 B9 B14 B15 B28; most common boot-killer

structural_rules.rule: On Google TV never disable launcherx or setupwraith, alone or together.
structural_rules.why: RecoveryActivity takes HOME; Wi-Fi and Cast credentials

structural_rules.rule: Never disable the current default IME (settings get secure default_input_method) or any enabled IME (ime list -s), or the IME Zapbar uses for typing.
Never disable a package whose dumpsys flags include PERSISTENT, or that is a core/system-UID app (sharedUserId android.uid.system).
structural_rules.why: hotelmode is PERSISTENT; persistent packages are started by system_server and others depend on them. General Android behaviour; no TV-specific breakage report beyond B18

structural_rules.rule: Never disable a package that holds android.permission.TV_INPUT_HARDWARE or that exports a TvInputService.
Never disable a package that answers the passthrough-channel VIEW intent (content://android.media.tv/passthrough/...) or android.settings.SETTINGS.
structural_rules.why: B21 (unverified origin); #92 shows HDMI routing uses this intent

structural_rules.rule: Never disable a package that answers android.intent.category.SETUP_WIZARD or whose name contains setupwizard, provision, or tvsetup (examples seen: com.mediatek.wwtv.setupwizard, com.xiaomi.android.tvsetup.partnercustomizer, com.google.android.tvsetup.partnercustomizer, com.android.provision, com.android.managedprovisioning, com.haier.tv.provision, com.amazon.tv.ffsprovisioneeclient).
structural_rules.why: #884 had a tvsetup package in a failing list (cause unverified). Category intent is Android knowledge, not CYTV

structural_rules.rule: Never disable packages that handle key events: those with an enabled AccessibilityService, an InputMethodService, a key-dispatch service (names like kpad, favkey, hotkey.dispatcher, uinputservice, remotepairing, inputinjection), or the vendor's keymap overlay.
structural_rules.why: remote and Input key die: B22, Hisense notes

structural_rules.rule: Never disable the current WebView provider (dumpsys webviewupdate).
structural_rules.why: Settings and apps embed WebView. No TV breakage report found; Android knowledge

structural_rules.rule: Never disable packages in the networking path: the connectivity resources, captive portal login, networkstack, Wi-Fi, Ethernet and DHCP vendor services.
structural_rules.why: TV can lose network; setupwraith owned Wi-Fi in B24. No direct breakage report for the others; precaution

structural_rules.rule: See never_exact. Also never disable the package that shows install prompts, or Zapbar's own sideload path breaks.
Never disable a package whose name or description says middleware, tvcenter, tvapi, tvservice, mal, or that holds a vendor TV-service binding.
Never launch or enable-toggle a package whose name says factory, production, AT or fac menu.
A package listed in a conditional dependency below is blocked whenever its dependent stays enabled.
After each disable, read back with pm list packages -d --user 0. Some firmware reports success while changing nothing, or re-enables at boot.
